coverage_note: State and local public employees under Va. Code 40.1-57.2 and 40.1-57.3. State agencies may not bargain; counties, cities, towns and local school boards may bargain only if they adopt an ordinance or resolution, which sets the local procedures. Constitutional officers and their employees are excluded. Local ordinances are not covered by this row.

governing_statute.value: Va. Code 40.1-57.2 and 40.1-57.3 (Collective Bargaining for Governmental Employees): bargaining is barred unless a county, city, town or school board authorizes it by local ordinance or resolution
governing_statute.quote: No state, county, city, town, or like governmental officer, agent, or governing body is vested with or possesses any authority to recognize any labor union or other employee association as a bargaining agent of any public officers or employees, or to collectively bargain or enter into any collective bargaining contract with any such union or association or its agents with respect to any matter relating to them or their employment or service unless, in the case of a county, city, or town, such authority is provided for or permitted by a local ordinance or by a resolution.

who_may_bargain.value: Employees of counties, cities, towns and local school boards whose governing body has adopted a bargaining ordinance or resolution; not state employees, and not constitutional officers or their employees
who_may_bargain.quote: if they are employees of a county, city, or town or local school board that has, by a local ordinance or resolution as provided in § 40.1-57.2 , authorized its employees to engage in collective bargaining, from doing so as provided in such ordinance or resolution.

strike_legality.value: Prohibited: a public employee who strikes in concert with two or more others is deemed to have terminated employment and is ineligible for public employment for 12 months
strike_legality.quote: strikes or willfully refuses to perform the duties of his employment shall, by such action, be deemed to have terminated his employment and shall thereafter be ineligible for employment in any position or capacity during the next 12 months by the Commonwealth

agency_fee_status.value: Prohibited. Virginia's right-to-work article applies to public employers and bars requiring dues or fees as a condition of employment; Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees.
agency_fee_status.quote: No employer shall require any person, as a condition of employment or continuation of employment, to pay any dues, fees or other charges of any kind to any labor union or labor organization.
